fact_check_verdict: PASS WITH CONDITIONS. One adversarial validator plus a showrunner read of the Nature abstract and a tally of the authors' Figshare inventory. Paper, TU Graz release (phys.org and tugraz.at, same release), Eurasia Review republication, Wikipedia for Vitus Lake. The validator advised no Alaska numbers on screen because no publication states them; declined on measurement: our tally reproduces the paper's global count exactly (10,118 to 13,685, +3,567), so Alaska counts from the same data are labelled OUR COUNT on every surface; area carries about; volume reserved.

claims.spoken: It's in Nature Climate Change, out November twentieth.
claims.verbatim_source: Nature page, labelled non-quotation: Published 20 November 2026, Nature Climate Change, Zhao et al.
requires: ordinal date, no year on screen

claims.spoken: Tobias Bolch, a co-author at TU Graz.
claims.verbatim_source: Nature author list, labelled non-quotation: Tobias Bolch, Graz University of Technology, co-author; first author Shaochun Zhao

claims.spoken: It mapped glacier lakes worldwide, in two thousand and in twenty twenty, with deep learning.
claims.verbatim_source: "by mapping glacial lakes worldwide in 2000 and 2020 using deep learning and manual refinement"
requires: circa 2000 and circa 2020, never exact years claimed as image dates

claims.spoken: The images were Landsat satellite pictures.
claims.verbatim_source: "The Landsat images used for glacial lake mapping are available from the US Geological Survey"

claims.spoken: Then people checked the lakes by hand.
claims.on_screen: CHECKED BY HAND · PER TU GRAZ
claims.verbatim_source: "Artificial intelligence was used to identify glacial lakes from the images, which were then checked manually."
requires: the AI did the first pass, people checked

claims.spoken: Worldwide, lakes touching glaciers rose by three thousand five hundred sixty-seven, about thirty-five percent.
claims.verbatim_source: "ice-contact lakes increased by 3,567 (+35%) in number"

claims.spoken: The study's press release calls Alaska's growth particularly pronounced, but prints no Alaska number.
claims.on_screen: "PARTICULARLY PRONOUNCED IN ALASKA ..." · PER TU GRAZ
claims.verbatim_source: "The expansion of the lakes was particularly pronounced in Alaska and the southern Andes."
requires: no Alaska number or split in the release or abstract

claims.spoken: The authors posted their whole lake map online.
claims.verbatim_source: Nature data availability, labelled non-quotation: the global glacial lake inventory for circa 2000 and 2020 is available via Figshare at doi 10.6084/m9.figshare.34332987

claims.spoken: The authors posted their map, so we counted. Our lake count matches theirs worldwide, exactly.
claims.verbatim_source: labelled non-quotation: our tally of the authors' Figshare inventory (global_glacial_lake_2000/2020 .dbf, Region and Type fields), script and output kept in runs/2026-11-28/glacier_lake_tally.txt: ice-contact (Type C) 10,118 in 2000, 13,685 in 2020

claims.spoken: By our count, Alaska's lakes touching glaciers went from nine hundred thirty-one to one thousand seventy-eight.
claims.verbatim_source: labelled non-quotation: our tally of the authors' Figshare inventory (global_glacial_lake_2000/2020 .dbf, Region and Type fields), script and output kept in runs/2026-11-28/glacier_lake_tally.txt: Region Alaska, Type C, 931 in 2000, 1,078 in 2020

claims.spoken: Their area grew about thirty-five percent, from about eight hundred eighty to about eleven hundred ninety square kilometers.
claims.on_screen: ALASKA · ABOUT 880 SQ KM · C. 2000 · OUR COUNT
claims.verbatim_source: labelled non-quotation: our tally of the authors' Figshare inventory (global_glacial_lake_2000/2020 .dbf, Region and Type fields), script and output kept in runs/2026-11-28/glacier_lake_tally.txt: Region Alaska, Type C, area 880.7 km2 in 2000, 1191.4 km2 in 2020

claims.spoken: Alaska's added area alone is about half the world's, by our count, from about one in thirteen of those lakes.
claims.on_screen: ABOUT HALF THE WORLD'S ADDED AREA · OUR COUNT
claims.verbatim_source: labelled non-quotation: our tally of the authors' Figshare inventory (global_glacial_lake_2000/2020 .dbf, Region and Type fields), script and output kept in runs/2026-11-28/glacier_lake_tally.txt: Alaska +310.7 km2 of world +636.6 km2 ice-contact area (paper's own world figure 604 +- 22 km2, so the share is 49 to 51 percent either way)

claims.spoken: Our count's biggest Alaska gain was Vitus Lake, at the foot of Bering Glacier. About a hundred five square kilometers became a hundred fifty-eight.
claims.on_screen: C. 2020 · ABOUT 158 SQ KM · OUR COUNT
claims.verbatim_source: labelled non-quotation: our tally of the authors' Figshare inventory (global_glacial_lake_2000/2020 .dbf, Region and Type fields), script and output kept in runs/2026-11-28/glacier_lake_tally.txt: Alaska's largest single ice-contact gain, inventory Group 92377, 104.9 to 158.0 km2, centroid 60.15 N 143.42 W, which is Vitus Lake (Wikipedia: Vitus Lake forms the southern limit of the Bering Lobe, Yakutat City and Borough)
requires: the study didn't single it out
at the southern edge of Bering Glacier's lobe

claims.spoken: Now the case for yes. Glaciers ending in a lake lost about sixty-six centimeters of water a year, on average. On land, about forty.
claims.on_screen: WORLDWIDE · LAKE-ENDING · ABOUT 66 CM A YEAR · ON AVERAGE
claims.verbatim_source: "lake-terminating glaciers experienced higher mass loss rates (-0.66 +- 0.16 m w.e. yr-1) than land- (-0.40 +- 0.12 m w.e. yr-1)"

claims.spoken: Bolch says contact with a lake further accelerates the loss of ice.
claims.on_screen: "CONTACT WITH A LAKE FURTHER ACCELERATES THE LOSS OF ICE" · TOBIAS BOLCH · PER TU GRAZ
claims.verbatim_source: "Our research has shown that contact with a lake further accelerates the loss of ice from a glacier,"

claims.spoken: Then the team's machine learning models weighed the factors.
claims.verbatim_source: "The research team used machine learning models to assess the impact of various factors on the glacier mass balance."

claims.spoken: For lake-ending glaciers worldwide, the lake explained about eleven percent of the ice loss. Climate, about forty-three. The glacier's own shape, about forty-six. A real push. The smallest of the three.
claims.verbatim_source: "Ice-contact lakes explain 11 +- 7% of the mass loss of lake-terminating glaciers globally, whereas climate forcing (43 +- 10%) and glacier geometry (46 +- 10%) are more relevant predictors for ice loss."

claims.spoken: The map stops at twenty twenty.
claims.verbatim_source: "mapping glacial lakes worldwide in 2000 and 2020"

claims.spoken: But their area grew only about nine percent.
Alaska has about one in thirteen of the world's lakes touching glaciers.
claims.verbatim_source: labelled non-quotation: our arithmetic on our tally of the authors' Figshare inventory, Alaska 1,078 of the world's 13,685 ice-contact lakes in 2020, 7.9 percent
